name: unigram evaluation perplexity
test:
import math
model = NGramCharModel(n=1).train("aab")
assert math.isclose(model.evaluate("ab"), math.sqrt(4.5), rel_tol=1e-9)
assert math.isinf(model.evaluate(""))
assert math.isinf(model.evaluate("az"))

name: bigram training resets previous state
test:
import math
model = NGramCharModel(n=2)
assert model.train("ababa") is model
assert math.isclose(model.evaluate("ab"), 1.0, rel_tol=1e-9)
model.train("bb")
assert math.isclose(model.evaluate("bb"), 1.0, rel_tol=1e-9)
assert math.isinf(model.evaluate("ab"))

name: generation uses frequency top one
test:
model = NGramCharModel(n=2).train("ababababac")
assert model.generate("a", max_new_chars=6) == "abababa"
assert model.generate("seed", max_new_chars=0) == "seed"
fallback = NGramCharModel(n=2).train("aaab")
assert fallback.generate("z", max_new_chars=3) == "zaaa"

name: invalid arguments and untrained behavior
input: n = 0, empty train text, untrained generation
test:
import math

def expect_value_error(callable_obj):
    try:
        callable_obj()
    except ValueError:
        return
    raise AssertionError("expected ValueError")

expect_value_error(lambda: NGramCharModel(n=0))
model = NGramCharModel()
expect_value_error(lambda: model.train(""))
expect_value_error(lambda: model.generate("", max_new_chars=1))
assert math.isinf(model.evaluate("abc"))
model.train("abc")
expect_value_error(lambda: model.generate("", max_new_chars=-1))

name: tiny Shakespeare train generate evaluate workflow
test:
import math
import os
from pathlib import Path

data_root = os.environ.get("DEEPCODE_DATA_PATH")
assert data_root, "DEEPCODE_DATA_PATH must point to a directory containing tiny_shakespeare.txt"
text = (Path(data_root) / "tiny_shakespeare.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace("\r\n", "\n")
assert len(text) >= 200, "tiny_shakespeare.txt is unexpectedly small"
model = NGramCharModel(n=4).train(text)
prompt = text[:20]
generated = model.generate(prompt, max_new_chars=80)
assert generated.startswith(prompt)
assert len(generated) == len(prompt) + 80
assert set(generated[len(prompt):]) <= set(text)
score = model.evaluate(text[:500])
assert math.isfinite(score)
assert score >= 1.0
